issues.problem: The prompt gives away its own answer. It calls magnesium hydroxide 'a mild, only slightly soluble base' and says it is 'a safer antacid than a strong base'. Learners are asked to explain exactly this, so the prompt should ask why it is safer without stating it.

It says that for magnesium hydroxide 'the pH stays near 10'. No lesson taught or measured this value. It is also the same pH as the soap solution (10.0), which the exemplar calls harmful if swallowed, so the safety reasoning contradicts itself. The exemplar should say that only a little dissolves, so it gives few OH- ions and raises the stomach pH only to about 3.5-5 (Lessons 7 and 9), and drop the pH 10 claim.
It says 80 minutes, but the phase times (Predict 8, Observe 28, Explain 20, DQB 7, Model Building 15) add up to 78 minutes, not 80.
